payload.direct_answer: The reviewed international clauses state that responsibility for AI systems must remain attributable to physical persons or existing legal entities, that humans decide whether to cede control in limited contexts and that AI can never replace ultimate human responsibility and accountability, and that appropriate oversight, impact assessment, audit and due diligence mechanisms should be developed to ensure accountability throughout the AI system life cycle. The UAE Charter clause states that human judgment and human oversight over AI are irreplaceable and may correct errors or biases, with a safeguard indicating health_service_operator review of automated lockouts where an AI output may be erroneous. The OECD clause states that AI actors should apply a systematic risk management approach to each phase of the AI system lifecycle on an ongoing basis, including co-operation between AI actors, suppliers, users and other stakeholders. No listed clause specifically addresses automatic lockouts of users.
